summary: Range lights from March 1893 at the mouth of the Ahnapee River; the red steel tower dates from 1932 and came off its pier for 2026 pier work.

access.note: Owned by the City of Algoma. Grounds open; tower closed to the public; the tower is on a detached breakwater.

events.note: Congress appropriated for 'Ahnapee range or pier lights' (LighthouseFriends dates the funding to March 1891)
Range lights (rear tower and post light) went into service 1 March 1893
Rear range tower: open framework below an enclosed upper section
Fifth-order lens replaced the lens lantern on the rear light (Board station entry: 5 June 1895; Board list of changes: 6 June 1895)
Bridge to the detached pier abandoned after elevated walkway installed
Electrically operated siren fog signal established 10 April 1910
Keeper Gustavus Umberham thrown overboard from the boat Reliance on the night of 3 February 1913 (LighthouseFriends only; no primary found)
Present steel tower placed on the pier in a $100,000 harbor improvement
Diaphone fog signal, operated by remote control
Deemed excess by the Coast Guard; offered under the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act
Fresnel lens removed; LED beacon installed
Catwalk removal began 18 May 2026 (Star-News). LighthouseFriends says the lighthouse was also removed; Star-News says it will be taken off later. Sources disagree.

corrections.why: The present tower was put on the pier in 1932 (USLHS: tower established 1932; LighthouseFriends). Neither source supports 1908 for this tower.
LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard removed the Fresnel lens in 2019; after restoration it went on display at North Point Lighthouse, Milwaukee.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS gives 1893 (range lights, first lit 1 March 1893 per the Board's 1893 report) and Wikidata gives 1932 (the present steel tower). Both are kept: 1893 is the first lighting; 1932 is the present tower.
Rowlett gives 1908 for a second tower. LighthouseFriends describes a wooden tower on the pier in 1910 and the steel tower of 1932. No checked source supports 1908 for this tower.
The Board's reports of 1891-1897 call it 'Ahnapee Pierhead Range'; USLHS lists Ahnapee Pierhead as an alternate name; LighthouseFriends says the town became Algoma a few years after 1871.
LighthouseFriends dates the bridge between the detached and shore cribs to 1892; the Board's report for the year ended 30 June 1893 records it. The story gives both.
The Board's 1891 appropriations list prints 'Ahnapee range or pier lights, Michigan'. The station is in Wisconsin (USLHS; 1892 and 1893 Board station entries). Treated as a misprint.
The Board's station entry gives 5 June 1895 and its list of changes gives 6 June 1895. The story gives both.

LighthouseFriends says the lighthouse and catwalk were removed as part of the 2026 pier project; the Star-News (22 May 2026) says the lighthouse 'will be taken off' when work is complete. Not reconciled; the story states both.

notes_for_editor: The 1913 drowning of keeper Gustavus Umberham rests on LighthouseFriends alone: no Board report, Life-Saving or Lighthouse Service bulletin entry and no Chronicling America hit for Wisconsin in 1913 were found. The story attributes it to LighthouseFriends and gives no death or search detail beyond that page. Re-check against a Kewaunee County newspaper before publishing. The 1891 appropriations list (FY1891 part of the bound 1891-1892 volume, scan p.24) prints the station's state as Michigan; the story says so. The 1895 lens date differs inside the Board's own report: station entry 5 June, list of changes 6 June. The story gives both. The 1893 bridge: the Board's FY1893 report records it; LighthouseFriends dates it 1892. The story gives both. The 2026 pier work: the Star-News (22 May 2026) says the lighthouse 'will be taken off'; LighthouseFriends says the lighthouse and catwalk were removed. Not reconciled. The pier work is attributed to Roen Salvage (Star-News); the Save the Catwalk site credits the US Army Corps of Engineers as the agency, and LighthouseFriends does not name a contractor. No report after May 2026 was read. The Board's 1892 appropriation figure for Ahnapee is illegible in the OCR, so the $2,500 figure is LighthouseFriends's and the story attributes it. Keeper rows are the USLHS roster (NARA registers via the Kraig Anderson inventory) and were not checked against primary keeper records; the 15 Coast Guard crew lines have no rank. Names matched by name, not position: the 1924-era and 1918-era OCR tables were not used for this station. The Board's life-saving station records for 'Ahnapee, Wis.' refer to a different station and are not used. Wikipedia was not cited.
